audit_metadata.claim_source: external claims atomicized from prompt text; no separate notes file available

claim_audit.claim: Main codec compatible is `qcom,wcd9378-codec`.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream OF match table contains `.compatible = "qcom,wcd9378-codec"`.

claim_audit.notes: Compatibility addition is plausible but must be reconciled with upstream binding constraints.

claim_audit.claim: Reset wiring is modeled with `qcom,wcd-rst-gpio-node` phandle.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream parser requires `qcom,wcd-rst-gpio-node`.
Upstream common schema requires `reset-gpios`, not `qcom,wcd-rst-gpio-node`.

claim_audit.notes: Treat as downstream board/property model; do not upstream as-is.

claim_audit.claim: Codec references SoundWire child nodes via `qcom,rx-slave` and `qcom,tx-slave`.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream code resolves slave nodes via `qcom,rx-slave`/`qcom,tx-slave`.
Upstream schema expects `qcom,rx-device`/`qcom,tx-device`.

claim_audit.notes: Property namespace differs from upstream and must be translated.

claim_audit.claim: SoundWire port/ch mapping is provided through `qcom,rx_swr_ch_map` and `qcom,tx_swr_ch_map`.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream probe consumes legacy SWR mapping properties.
Upstream SDW binding defines `qcom,tx-port-mapping` and `qcom,rx-port-mapping` instead.

claim_audit.notes: Downstream map format is not schema-compatible with upstream SDW properties.

claim_audit.claim: `qcom,swr-tx-port-params` DT property is required for functional TX setup.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream parser expects and validates `qcom,swr-tx-port-params`.
No `qcom,swr-tx-port-params` property is defined in upstream SDW schema.

claim_audit.notes: May imply binding extension or removable downstream detail; cannot decide without extra functional evidence.

claim_audit.claim: Micbias values are expected as `qcom,cdc-micbias*-mv` properties.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream parser reads `qcom,cdc-micbias[1-3]-mv`.
Upstream schema names are `qcom,micbias*-microvolt` and includes micbias4.

claim_audit.notes: Property naming/units differ; convert to common schema.

claim_audit.claim: Upstream `qcom,wcd937x*.yaml` can be used as-is with no binding adjustments.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Upstream main compatible set is restricted to wcd9370/wcd9375 variants.
Downstream declares a distinct compatible `qcom,wcd9378-codec`.
Downstream uses DT properties absent from upstream binding set.

claim_audit.notes: At minimum, compatibility and property mapping work is required before claiming schema coverage.

claim_audit.claim: WCD9378 downstream path depends on Qualcomm SWR stack (`<soc/soundwire.h>`) rather than upstream Linux SDW APIs.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Includes downstream header `<soc/soundwire.h>`.
Slave driver also includes `<soc/soundwire.h>`.
Upstream reference uses Linux SDW headers (`<linux/soundwire/...>`).

claim_audit.notes: Confirms required API family migration, not necessarily SoundWire core modification.

claim_audit.claim: RX/TX slave paging must be enabled (`paging_support = true`).

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream explicitly sets `paging_support = true` on both slave devices.
Downstream SWR device struct contains `paging_support` field.

claim_audit.notes: Requirement is confirmed only for downstream SWR stack; upstream SDW equivalent behavior is unclear.

claim_audit.claim: Legacy SWR APIs (`swr_driver_register`, `swr_get_logical_dev_num`) are required for probe/bind flow.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Slave bind/init path uses these downstream SWR APIs.
Defines and exports the referenced SWR APIs.

claim_audit.notes: Confirms downstream dependence; conversion must remove these calls in favor of upstream SDW model.

claim_audit.claim: Upstream SoundWire core changes are required before WCD9378 can be upstreamed.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: No WCD9378-specific logic appears in core controller driver excerpt.
Upstream WCD937x uses existing SDW stack without codec-specific core patches in this flow.

claim_audit.notes: Core-change necessity cannot be proven from available evidence; treat as fail-closed until concrete blocker is identified.

claim_audit.claim: WCD9378 bring-up requires source changes in LPASS RX/TX macro drivers.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: No WCD9378-specific references are present in inspected LPASS RX macro content.
No direct WCD9378 coupling found in allowed LPASS TX source scan.

claim_audit.notes: No concrete LPASS modification requirement is evidenced in allowed sources.

claim_audit.claim: No direct WCD9378-specific coupling exists inside upstream LPASS RX/TX macro source files.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Inspected sections are generic LPASS macro code, not WCD codec-specific wiring.
Search found no WCD9378 symbol references.

claim_audit.notes: Absence of direct references supports avoiding speculative LPASS edits.

claim_audit.claim: WCD9378 codec path requires Class-H control and routing.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream has Class-H DAPM supply/event and class-h init call.

claim_audit.notes: Class-H behavior is real; API shape must be converted to upstream model.

claim_audit.claim: Upstream `wcd-clsh-v2` must gain a dedicated WCD9378 codec version enum.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Enum includes WCD937X/WCD938X/WCD939X but no explicit WCD9378 entry.
Downstream uses legacy class-h header, so direct mapping choice is unclear.

claim_audit.notes: Cannot assert enum extension necessity without proving WCD937X mode is insufficient.

claim_audit.claim: Downstream Class-H API usage must be mapped from legacy `wcd_cls_h_*` to upstream v2 control interface.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Uses legacy `wcd_cls_h_init` API.
Upstream class-h interface is `wcd_clsh_ctrl_*` based.

claim_audit.notes: API migration is likely required; exact per-event mapping still needs concrete conversion design.

claim_audit.claim: Downstream SDW slave identity is `qcom,wcd9378-slave` / `wcd9378-slave`.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Both id-table and OF match define the downstream slave identity.

claim_audit.notes: Identity differs from upstream schema and requires compatibility strategy.

claim_audit.claim: Upstream-compatible SDW identity should align to `sdw20217010a00` style binding.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Binding defines SDW compatible constant as `sdw20217010a00`.
Upstream WCD937x SDW device ID is represented via SDW slave entry table.

claim_audit.notes: Whether WCD9378 shares the same SDW id still requires hardware evidence.

claim_audit.claim: Slave debugfs peek/poke/register-dump hooks are required for upstream functionality.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Debugfs nodes are created only under `CONFIG_DEBUG_FS` (`swrslave_peek/poke/reg_dump`).
Additional SDCA debugfs register poking infrastructure is debug-centric.

claim_audit.notes: Keep for local bring-up only; exclude from upstream functional requirements.

claim_audit.claim: SDW implementation should follow upstream pattern with `devm_regmap_init_sdw` and Linux SDW component flow.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Upstream probe uses `devm_regmap_init_sdw` and component integration with runtime PM.
Downstream currently uses `devm_regmap_init_swr` (legacy stack), confirming migration target.

claim_audit.notes: This is a clear architectural migration item.

claim_audit.claim: Current codec file includes vendor-only dependencies that are not upstreamable.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Includes kernel-version guards, MSM CDC frameworks, vendor bindings, QTI debugfs, bolero internals.

claim_audit.notes: High-confidence cleanup requirement for upstreamability.

claim_audit.claim: Regulator handling must move from `msm_cdc_*` helpers to upstream regulator APIs.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream probe uses MSM CDC supply init/enable helpers.
Upstream reference uses named supply list with `devm_regulator_bulk_get_enable`.

claim_audit.notes: Deterministic API migration item.

claim_audit.claim: Reset handling must move from vendor pinctrl/reset-node handling to upstream GPIO reset model.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream reset flow depends on vendor pinctrl state and reset-node phandle.
Upstream model uses `devm_gpiod_get` for reset handling.

claim_audit.notes: Deterministic model change with strong reference signal.

claim_audit.claim: MBHC behavior should be represented via shared `wcd-mbhc-v2` model with codec-specific callbacks only.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Downstream has local wrapper but still delegates to `wcd_mbhc_init` with callback table.
Upstream uses shared MBHC callback model and common init API.

claim_audit.notes: Shared-module direction is clear, but exact callback set and wrapper retention still need triage.

claim_audit.claim: WCD9378 register and DAPM surface area is large and requires explicit triage before conversion.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Controls/widgets/routes are large (27/129/72).
`#define WCD9378_*` count is high (856), showing large register surface.
Mask define count is 1736, reinforcing large register/mask footprint.

claim_audit.notes: Large-scale translation must be scoped and prioritized to avoid speculative carry-over.

claim_audit.claim: QTI regmap/debugfs and SDCA debugfs helpers are needed only for bring-up debug, not upstream driver function.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Registers QTI and SDCA debugfs hooks after probe.
Implements debugfs address/data/register manipulation files.

claim_audit.notes: Treat as local diagnostics, not conversion target behavior.

claim_audit.claim: Temporary bring-up prints/debug paths should be excluded from upstream patching scope.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Contains bring-up style `dev_err(... "wcd irq init done")` informational print.
Debugfs bring-up entries reinforce debug-only nature.

claim_audit.notes: Explicitly keep debug-only artifacts out of upstream patch plan.

claim_audit.claim: External bring-up playback is confirmed working.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: No concrete runtime logs, command output, or trace artifacts were provided in allowed sources.
Driver source shows code paths but not proof of successful end-to-end playback on hardware.

claim_audit.notes: Need reproducible runtime evidence before treating playback as validated.

claim_audit.claim: External bring-up capture is confirmed working.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: No capture logs or validated capture command traces were provided.
Code existence is not equivalent to runtime capture proof.

claim_audit.notes: Capture status must be validated with reproducible runtime evidence.

claim_audit.claim: Any mute-path runtime issue is fully resolved.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: Contains dedicated mute checks and conditional mute writes, indicating sensitivity in mute sequencing paths.
No definitive runtime artifact demonstrates issue closure across playback/capture conditions.

claim_audit.notes: Treat mute-status claims as unresolved until validated with deterministic runtime tests.

evidence.why_it_supports_or_rejects: No command recipe artifacts are present in inspected source trees.
